correctness.rationale: The norm is exactly kernel L1; an oscillatory phase-average limit exists by Riemann–Lebesgue on compact subsets away from the origin, with global domination |difference|<=|h|. The central-deletion integral evaluates to 1/2−4log(2)/π²; numerical checks are supplementary and not the proof.

value.rationale: Deleting frequencies is a canonical sharp endpoint stability operation; despite both norms growing logarithmically, every fixed nonempty notch has a strictly positive order-one cost, and the most natural notch (the mean) has a simple exact universal constant. The theorem identifies a structurally nontrivial, scale-independent obstruction rather than a routine recalculation of the leading logarithmic divergence.
